Commentary.Commentary: Kumar was the standout bowler as he along with Bumrah ran through the top order. They were well supported by the rest. Everybody except for Kedar Jadhav who was very economical chipped in with wickets. The surface is a little tricky but as Kohli said at the toss it might ease out in the second half under lights. The tourists will have to bowl really well if they are to defend this total. The Indian batting line-up on the other hand will fancy themselves to chase this down and level the series. Join us in a while for the chase.

Brilliant bowling performance by India! They will be happier of the two sides heading into the break. New Zealand after winning the toss and electing to bat got off to a poor start as they lost their top three for not much. The Taylor-Latham partnership also could not provide stability as the former departed cheaply. Nicholls along with Tom Latham did steady the ship for them with a 60-run stand but a flurry of wickets in the end pulled back the Kiwis. A cameo first from de Grandhomme and later from Southee has given their bowlers something to bowl at.

The decision stands, though New Zealand don't lose a review as it is umpire's call. Williamson's uncomfortable short stay comes to an end. This is also the first time since 2013 that he has had back-to-back single digit scores in ODIs. The visitors are in trouble here.

Shorter in length but outside off, Munro gets on top of the bounce and guides it down to third man for a run.
Just short of a length on off, Munro defends it towards point.
Now comes around the wicket as Bumrah tries to create a diffrent angle. He lands it on a length on off, Munro defends it off the front foot.

Fuller in length on middle, Williamson times it straight down the ground. Patel runs to his left from mid on and dives. He makes a half-stop but recovers well and keeps it down to two. Good effort by the left arm spinner.
Good length on off, Williamson defends it off the front foot.
BEATEN! Kumar bowls it on a length outside off, the ball skids off the surface. Williamson tries to guide it down to third man but gets beaten. That could have easily taken the edge.
Fuller in length on off, Williamson drives it towards mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flicks it towards fine leg for a run.
A catching short mid-wicket in place.
A well-disguised slower ball outside off, Williamson failed to pick it and gets an inside edge as he tries to defend it. A maiden by Bumrah, good comeback.
Angles it into the pads. Williamson flicks it to mid-wicket.
Good length on off, Williamson defends it towards point.
Bowls it from wide of the crease and pitches it on the line of off. Williamson lunges forward in defense.
Shorter in length, a little width on offer. Williamson cuts it to point.
Bumrah bowls it on a length on off, Williamson defends it off the front foot.
Angles it onto the pads, too easy for Williamson as he flicks it towards fine leg to get off the mark.
Lands it on a length around off, Kane defends it off the front foot.
Kane Williamson, the skipper, is the next man in.

OUT! Kumar draws first blood! Guptill the dangerman is walking back. A very good delivery by Bhuvneshwar. He goes wide of the crease and lands it on a length around off, straightens after pitching. Guptill pokes at it away from his body and gets a faint outside edge to Dhoni who takes a good low catch. An early wicket for India, just what they needed. Bhuvi is all pumped up and so are the Indians. Guptill's poor record on Asian soil continues.
Back of a length outside off, Munro guides it down to third man for a run.

SIX! BANG! This is what you will get from these two attacking batsmen! Expecting Kumar to bowl a length ball, Munro comes down the track, gets to the pitch of it and hits it straight back over the bowler's head for a maximum.
Length on off, Munro tries to drive it on the up but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

JAFFA! A good comeback, nice way to end the over. He lands it on a length from wide of the crease. Comes in with the angle and straightens after pitching. Guptill tries to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge. A good over for New Zealand, 11 from it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! A hit-me ball by Bumrah! Short and wide outside off, width on offer. Guptill cuts it through point and into the fence.
FOUR! First boundary of the day! Shorter in length by Bumrah outside off, Guptill rocks onto the back foot and punches it through cover-point for a boundary.
Fuller in length on off, Guptill leans into it and drives it through the gap between extra cover and mid off. Kohli there gives it a chase and keeps it down to two.
Errs in line and bowls it on the pads. Munro fails to flick and it goes off the pads towards square leg for a leg bye.
Jasprit Bumrah will bowl with the second new ball.
Good length on off, Guptill defends it off the front foot. Two from the first over. A good one by Kumar.
A surprise bouncer, comes quick onto the batsman. Munro pulls it but not off the middle down to fine leg for a run to get off the mark.
Just ahead of a length on off, slanting across this time. Munro defends it solidly.
Fuller in length on off, shaping back in. Munro tries to drive but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

New Zealand are away! A similar length by Bhuvi, this time closer to the off pole. Guptill drives it towards covers where the fielder makes a half-stop and concedes a run. The fielder from mid off who did the mopping up job did score a direct hit at the striker's end but the batsman was easily in.
Swing for Bhuvneshwar! He comes running in and lands it on a length outside off, it shapes away further. Guptill plants his front foot ahead and leaves it.

Both the teams are out for their respective national anthems. New Zealand's anthem will be sung first followed by India's. We have finished with the national anthems and we are all set to get underway. Martin Guptill and Colin Munro will open the batting for New Zealand. They would hope they can provide a good start. Bhuvneshwar Kumar will bowl with the first new ball. A early wicket is what India want from him. He has two slips in place for him. Here we go...

India skipper, Virat Kohli says they wanted to field anyway. He reckons it is a good surface to bat on. He further adds the wicket gets better in the evening and it will be on the slower side in the afternoon. Mentions the morale in the dressing room is still high as they have won 9 out of their last 11 games. Informs there is one change, Axar Patel comes in for Kuldeep Yadav.

New Zealand skipper, Kane Williamson says, they want to bat first. Mentions the performance in the last game was very good and they would want to replicate the same today. Reckons it is very hot today and he hopes that his players can adjust to the conditions. Ends by saying they are playing the same side.
TOSS - New Zealand win the toss and they opt to bat first.

The visitors on the other hand, will head into the match high on confidence and they also have momentum on their side. Kane Williamson would hope they can replicate their performance and clinch the series today. A lot is at stake for both the sides and we can expect a cracker. Stay tuned for the toss and teams in a while.

Hello and welcome to the 2nd ODI between India and New Zealand in Pune. Both the teams are playing their 100th one-dayer against each other. The hosts will be eager to bounce back after a shock defeat in the first game. Virat Kohli would hope that every one stands up and delivers the goods. It will be interesting to see if they make any changes to their playing eleven which has been so successful in the recent past.
